description: Hand-derived vectors for the Make it postable planner's tone (prompt version 6, plan version 3; doc/spec/ai.md sections 16.3 and 16.5). The transcript is plan-validation-cases.json's (30 items); each reply is its valid-clip reply with the version 2 fields neutral and tone/toneSummary set. 'tone' is the request's tone: null (no tone line), {mode: auto} offering every catalogue tone in order, {mode: as-said}, or {mode: fixed, id} naming a catalogue tone or 'savedTones'. 'expect.tone' is [id, title, summary] or null; 'repairs' lists [field, action] pairs sorted. 'instructions' pins the tone line a clip instruction for [0, 29] ends with. Edit by hand and replay it in every Core suite that implements the planner.

instructions.endsWith: Tone: Viral YouTuber. The creator chose it for this clip: write its rewrites, title, hook and post text in it, and set tone to "viral-youtuber". In their words: Rewrite it the way a top YouTuber would say it. Put a hook in the first sentence that makes a stranger stop scrolling, by rewording my opening rather than adding a line before it. Then short, punchy sentences, one thought each. Where attention would dip, make a pattern interrupt by turning a line into a sharp question or a quick turn. Build to one clear payoff and land it. Energetic but natural, like me on my best take, never hype for its own sake. Make it tighter by cutting rather than adding: each rewritten phrase is as long as the words it replaces or shorter, never longer, because the video keeps running under it. Never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.

Tone: My pitch voice. The creator chose it for this clip: write its rewrites, title, hook and post text in it, and set tone to "my-pitch-voice". In their words: Sound like my investor pitch: confident, specific, one number per line. Keep my facts.
Tone: as the creator said it. Keep their own tone and set tone to "none".

Tone: choose the one that suits this clip best, or none, and set tone to its id or "none". The tones:
- viral-youtuber: Viral YouTuber (hook, punchy, payoff). Rewrite it the way a top YouTuber would say it. Put a hook in the first sentence that makes a stranger stop scrolling, by rewording my opening rather than adding a line before it. Then short, punchy sentences, one thought each. Where attention would dip, make a pattern interrupt by turning a line into a sharp question or a quick turn. Build to one clear payoff and land it. Energetic but natural, like me on my best take, never hype for its own sake. Make it tighter by cutting rather than adding: each rewritten phrase is as long as the words it replaces or shorter, never longer, because the video keeps running under it. Never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.
- punchy-reel: Punchy Reel (≤ 30 s, fast cuts). Make it a fast Reel that runs under 30 seconds. Start on the most surprising line, cut every word that does not earn its place, and keep one idea per sentence. Short, rhythmic lines that build to a quick, memorable ending. Make it tighter by cutting rather than adding: each rewritten phrase is as long as the words it replaces or shorter, never longer, because the video keeps running under it. Never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.
- storyteller: Storyteller (setup, tension, payoff). Tell it as a story. A quick setup that puts the listener in the moment, then the problem or tension, then the turn and the payoff. Use the concrete details I already gave, in plain spoken words. Warm and vivid, never dramatic for its own sake. Each rewritten phrase must take no longer to say than the words it replaces, because the video keeps running under it. Shorter is fine; never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.
- clear-explainer: Clear explainer (step by step). Make it easy to follow. Say the point first, then explain it step by step in plain words, one idea per sentence. Swap jargon for everyday words unless the term matters, and end with what it means for the listener. Each rewritten phrase must take no longer to say than the words it replaces, because the video keeps running under it. Shorter is fine; never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.
- linkedin-pro: LinkedIn pro (calm, credible). Make it sound like a credible professional on LinkedIn. Open with the insight, back it with what I actually did or saw, and end with a takeaway people can use. Calm, confident and specific. No buzzwords, humblebrag or clickbait. Each rewritten phrase must take no longer to say than the words it replaces, because the video keeps running under it. Shorter is fine; never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.
- funny: Funny (light, one joke). Make it light and funny. Keep my point, and turn one line into a well-placed joke or witty turn of phrase that grows out of what I said, ideally near the end. Playful and warm, never mean, sarcastic or forced. Each rewritten phrase must take no longer to say than the words it replaces, because the video keeps running under it. Shorter is fine; never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.
- hype-launch: Hype launch (big news, clear ask). Make it a launch announcement. Lead with the news, say who it is for and why it matters now, and end with one clear call to action. Excited and confident, with real energy, but every claim stays exactly as true as what I said. Each rewritten phrase must take no longer to say than the words it replaces, because the video keeps running under it. Shorter is fine; never pad with filler words or connectors. Keep my facts, names, numbers and meaning, and keep my voice. Every line must be speakable as is: no emoji, hashtags, links or stage directions.
- calm-sincere: Calm & sincere (honest, unhurried). Make it calm and sincere. Unhurried sentences, honest and personal, as if I were speaking to one person I respect. Remove hype, filler and exaggeration, and let the point land quietly. Make it tighter by cutting rather than adding: each rewritten phrase is as long as the words it replaces or shorter, never longer, because the video keeps running under it.
